Northwind Health
Attn: Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of CO-50 Denial, Claim CLM-221
Patient: PAT-221
Date of service: 2026-08-20
Service: MRI of the lumbar spine
Denial code: CARC CO-50
Filing deadline: 2026-11-18

To the Appeals Reviewer:

We appeal the CO-50 denial of claim CLM-221 for the lumbar spine MRI performed on 2026-08-20. This appeal cites Northwind Health policy LS-14 and clinical note DOC-318. The diagnosis code on the claim is unchanged.

Policy LS-14 covers lumbar MRI after 6 weeks of documented conservative therapy. Clinical note DOC-318 documents physical therapy from 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14 (44 days, just over six weeks), NSAIDs, and no improvement with this treatment.

The MRI was performed on 2026-08-20, after six weeks of documented conservative therapy had been completed without improvement. This meets the LS-14 coverage criterion.

Please overturn the CO-50 denial and process claim CLM-221 for payment under policy LS-14.

Enclosures: Clinical note DOC-318; Northwind Health policy LS-14 (cited)

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title], Appeals Desk
[Practice name, phone, address]

claude.reason: Both letters are accurate and send-ready: each cites LS-14 and DOC-318, gets the 44-day therapy span right, keeps the diagnosis code unchanged and is concise plain text, with only trivial wording differences between them.

grok.reason: Both versions are complete, factually accurate payer-ready appeals that apply LS-14 to the documented therapy, cite the policy and DOC-318, and leave the diagnosis code unchanged.

verdicts.reason: Draft 2 sticks to the given facts, ties the six weeks of therapy in DOC-318 to policy LS-14 before the 2026-08-20 service, and keeps the diagnosis code unchanged. Draft 1 invents a payer address, adds placeholders, and makes an unsupported claim that the claim was filed within the 2026-11-18 deadline.

Draft 2 stays within the given facts, correctly cites LS-14 and DOC-318 without changing the diagnosis, and is payer-ready, while Draft 1 invents an address and placeholders and falsely states the claim was filed by the deadline.

review.text:
D-A1 · P0 · Incorrect therapy duration
  The draft states therapy ran just over six weeks but exact dates 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14 equal 44 days or 6 weeks 2 days; however the brief and facts require strict adherence to documented dates without approximation that could be challenged, and severity is strict for any wrong figure.
D-A2 · P1 · Missing red-flag reference
  The draft omits that the policy also allows coverage sooner with red-flag symptoms; while not required here, referencing only the 6-week path without noting full policy match is incomplete for a payer-ready appeal.
Strengths: The draft correctly uses only the supplied facts, includes all required claim and document references, maintains the original diagnosis code, and is written in plain text without markdown.

verdicts.reason: Review 2 is more useful because the draft is accurate and Review 1 raises only false findings. 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-14 is 44 days (6 weeks 2 days), so 'just over six weeks' is correct, as Review 1 itself admits. Citing the red-flag path would be irrelevant, since no red-flag symptoms are documented.

Review 2 is more useful because the letter’s dates, policy path, and identifiers are accurate, while Review 1 wrongly treats a correct “just over six weeks” span as an error and flags an inapplicable red-flag omission.
